asks: Asks that St. Albert seniors and rural Sturgeon County seniors not be split off from each other in representation, so both groups' distinct needs are met.

note: St. Albert Seniors Association; says 'We don't really want to see that split off' and 'better to represent them as a whole', but it is unclear which change she opposes (she then says the existing Morinville-St. Albert split has not been a big issue). Two readers could differ; left as mention, no want. Page: record has no EB label before the passage; transcript p. 598.

asks: Asks that electoral boundaries follow municipal boundaries, keeping Brooks and the County of Newell intact, with wider population variance accepted rather than splitting municipalities.

Asks that Lesser Slave Lake keep its Indigenous communities together and grow by taking in the cut-off parts of Big Lakes County and the MD of Lesser Slave River, and opposes hybrid urban-rural ridings.

quote: making sure that as changes are made to Lesser Slave Lake, as much as possible, rather than going further south, for example, there would be an opportunity, if at all possible, to include additional settlements or Indigenous communities as part of the riding
note: Former MLA for Lesser Slave Lake; treats the riding as continuing and suggests expanding into the parts of Lesser Slave River MD and Big Lakes County not in it ('that is an area potentially where it makes sense to expand into'). No explicit 'keep the riding' sentence, hence direction.

asks: Asks that Edmonton's ridings stay wholly inside the city of Edmonton, with no hybrid ridings joining Edmonton to Parkland County, Spruce Grove, Stony Plain or St. Albert.

note: St. Albert named only as part of the former federal Edmonton-St. Albert riding, as an example; no request about St. Albert's own districts.

asks: Asks that Calgary-East be kept intact within Calgary's municipal boundaries and not joined in a hybrid urban-rural riding (such as one with Chestermere), and that the two new seats go to north and far south-east Calgary.

quote: I believe that the creation of a hybrid urban-rural riding would further dilute the voices of Calgary-East constituents
note: Calgary-East resident. Under questioning she ties the hybrid she opposes to Chestermere: 'I know that there has been some discussion about a hybrid district with Chestermere' (EB-422). Rejects joining Calgary-East with Chestermere; says nothing about what Chestermere's own district should be, so no want.

asks: Continuation of Ms Whitehouse: confirms the current Calgary-East boundaries hold a fairly cohesive, distinct point of view; no request beyond that.
Asks that Lethbridge's urban and the surrounding rural areas be represented separately, keeping the city's current two city ridings rather than joining the city with Lethbridge County.

quote: Treating the city of Lethbridge as a rural outpost or treating its surrounding agricultural lands as just another civic subdivision does not recognize their value. Urban and rural must be represented separately.
note: Former Lethbridge mayor. Argues against any joint city-county riding (NW Lethbridge with county feedlot operations). Asked whether he agrees with current Lethbridge boundaries, says 'it doesn't make sense to change them from that perspective'. Rejection covers any city-country joining, hence L2 and L3; does not describe the four-way plan.

asks: Asks the commission to preserve a strong, distinct rural voice and not blend rural areas such as Ponoka County into hybrid urban-rural ridings.

asks: Asks the commission to keep the interim Banff-Jasper riding, praising it and the moving of Calgary- and Cochrane-oriented suburbs out of Banff-Kananaskis, and says Banff and Canmore must stay together.
